title: Require git 2.43, and report a merge git cannot run as an error, not a conflict
prompt:
GitHub issue #5: https://github.com/acupof-ai/Spawn/issues/5. Read it, then `MIN_GIT`, `check_git_version` and `require_git` in crates/spawn-cli/src/config.rs (and its tests), their callers in crates/spawn-cli/src/runtime.rs and crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, `landing_candidate` and its caller in `judge()` in integrate.rs, and README.md's requirements table.

The problem. Merges take main's merge rules from its `.gitattributes` with the global option `git --attr-source=<main>`. That option first appeared in Git 2.41.0 (its release notes: "git --attr-source=<tree> cmd $args" is new). Git 2.43.0's release notes record that "git merge-tree" used to segfault when the "--attr-source" option was used. The start-up check accepts 2.40 (`MIN_GIT = (2, 40)`, and its comment wrongly says 2.40 introduced the option). README says "2.40 or later". So on git 2.40 to 2.42 the check passes and the merge fails (exit 129 for the unknown option on 2.40, a crash on 2.41 and 2.42). The integrator's `landing_candidate` turns every failure of that `merge-tree` into `Ok(None)`, which `judge()` records as a gate `conflict` and sends back to the worker with instructions to resolve conflict markers that do not exist. The task can never land, and the operator is never told to upgrade git. The issue is right on all of this. Only the line numbers have moved. The Bridge's own merge of main (crates/spawn-host/src/git.rs) already tells exit 1 (a conflict) from other failures.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks):
1. `MIN_GIT` is 2.43. `spawn tick` and `spawn integrate` (and everything else that checks git at start) refuse an older git with a non-zero exit and a message that names 2.43. A git answering `git version 2.43.0` or later is accepted. Correct the comment. Update config.rs's tests (2.42 refused, 2.43 accepted).
2. README.md states the requirement as "2.43 or later".
3. In `landing_candidate`, a `merge-tree` that exits 1 is a conflict, as now. Any other failure (exit 129, a crash or signal, any other code) is an error that reaches the operator with git's own message, never a conflict. No gate verdict is recorded for the task. It stays as it was (`reported`, no revision counted), nothing is sent to its worker, and a later integrator pass tries again. Add a unit test for the classification.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/008.sh (read it), run from the root of your tree.
(a) README.md must contain "2.43 or later". With a `git` first in PATH that answers `git version 2.42.0` and passes every other call to the real git, `spawn tick` and `spawn integrate --once` must exit non-zero with output naming 2.43. With one answering `git version 2.43.0`, and with the real git, both must run.
(b) As in 004.sh: a gated mission, a recording gate, a real Bridge with a fake engine whose work the pusher publishes to a local source. The source's main then moves, so landing needs a merge. One `spawn integrate --once` pass runs with a `git` that fails every `merge-tree` carrying `--attr-source` (exit 129, "unknown option: --attr-source=...") and passes everything else on. After it: no `task.gated` record for the task, the task still `reported` with 0 revisions, main unmoved, and the pass's output containing "unknown option". A second pass with the real git must land the task: main holds the worker's file and main's own change.
It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure (it needs a real git 2.43 or later).

Not part of this objective: the conflict note in `judge()` still says main is merged into the workspace when a turn ends and while the worker is idle, which is no longer how merges of main work (main reaches a branch only when an execution starts or resumes, docs/storage.md). Leave it unless you touch that text anyway.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
